responses:
The test now passes and the fix is committed to `feat/quote-pdf` as `f680134`. The full suite passes (11 tests).

**Cause:** the test was written ahead of the feature (it was in a "WIP" commit). The export template never added an `@font-face` rule, but ADR-0007 says Arabic quotes must use an embedded font from `app/fonts/`, never a system font.

**Fix (`app/pdf.py`):**
- Arabic quotes now get a `<head><style>` block. It has an `@font-face` rule for "Noto Naskh Arabic" pointing at `app/fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf`, and sets that font on `body`.
- The font is found relative to the module, so it doesn't depend on the working directory.
- English quotes are unchanged.

**Test (`tests/test_rtl_font.py`):** the old check only looked for the text `@font-face`, so a rule pointing at any font would have passed. It now also checks that the rule points at the bundled file and that the font is applied. I added a second test that the font file exists.

**Before this ships:** `app/fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf` isn't a real font. It's a 117-byte text file that says "SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER… Not a real font." The tests pass because they only check the HTML. A real PDF export would fail to load this font or fall back to another one, so the actual Noto Naskh Arabic TTF needs to replace it.
